CLI reference

ovmanager is the operator CLI for the panel. It is installed with the panel, lives next to it in /opt/ovmanager, and is refreshed on every update. Run it with no arguments for the same list you find here.

Everything needs root on the panel server

Every ovmanager command — including the read-only ones — reads /opt/ovmanager/.env, which holds the secret panel URL path, the bind address and the data directory. Run sudo ovmanager <command>. The only exceptions are ovmanager, ovmanager help and ovmanager --help, which print usage without touching the config. The panel itself needs no root: any account can log in to the web UI.

Commands (panel server)

Compiled from make build and ovmanager --help.
CommandWhat it does
ovmanagerPrint the command list and exit.
ovmanager status [--all]Service, health, version and the panel URL. --all also shows mode, port, data and install paths.
ovmanager service start | stop | restartService control.
ovmanager service enable | disableAutomatic start at boot.
ovmanager logs [N|-f]The last N log lines (default 100), or follow live.
ovmanager backup [--keep N]Write a verified database backup now. --keep sets retention, 1–500, default 14 (the installer's daily timer pins 7).
ovmanager restore [NAME]List the available backups, or restore one by name.
ovmanager urlpathPrint the secret URL prefix the panel is served under.
ovmanager tlsInteractive TLS menu: status, issue (Let's Encrypt), renew, remove, self-signed, custom install.
ovmanager updateStaged update with automatic failover. Recovers an update interrupted by a reboot or power loss before starting a new one.
ovmanager reset-passwordSet a new owner password, then restart the panel.
ovmanager completion bash | zsh | fishInstall shell completion and print the line to source.

Options

OptionApplies to
-y, --yesNever prompt.
-a, --allstatus — include paths and mode.
--keep Nbackup — how many backups to keep (1–500, default 14).
--purgeuninstall — also delete data and certificates.
-v, --version Vupdate — pin a release, e.g. -v v2.0.0.
-h, --helpHelp.

Configuration

The panel reads /opt/ovmanager/.env. The installer writes a minimal file (HOST, PORT, URLPATH, ADMIN_USERNAME, DATA_DIR) and sets no secrets there — the owner password is a bcrypt hash in the database, never in .env. The documented variables are:

VariableEffect
HOSTBind address the panel listens on (default 127.0.0.1).
PORTListen port (default 2095).
URLPATHSecret URL prefix (default dashboard); leave empty for the default.
ADMIN_USERNAMEWhich database row is the owner (default admin).
DATA_DIRDatabase, backups and node material (default /var/lib/ovmanager, mode 0700).
OVMANAGER_LIVE_POLL_SECONDSLive poll interval for the dashboard collector.
OVM_TRAFFIC_POLL_SECONDSTraffic polling interval.
OVM_METRICS_INTERVAL_SECONDSMetrics collection interval.
TRUSTED_PROXYRead real client IPs from X-Forwarded-For when behind your own nginx/Caddy/Cloudflare.
OVM_REPORelease source for ovmanager update (fork, e.g. myorg/OVManager).
OVM_ACME_DOMAINDomain for the built-in Let's Encrypt issuance.

The installer (install.sh)

install.sh answers to subcommands and to a small flag set. Everything that shapes an install is an OVM_* variable with the same value in interactive and scripted runs, so the two cannot disagree.

The installer downloads a release binary for the platform and installs it as a systemd service with a daily backup timer, starts the panel and health-checks it. The panel URL and claim key are shown after the optional node installer and before following logs. There is no Docker mode: the installer is native systemd only.

On each VPN node

The node agent installs its own CLI, ovnode. The full command list lives in the OVNode repository (ovnode help --all on the node). The panel's operator view is kept here; the node side is kept in the OVNode project. Deprecated node names are listed in ovnode help --all with a deprecation note.
